name: x86-align-branch-boundary
rationale: Instruction, register, cache and ABI properties differ by CPU; use target-specific costs and measure ARM and x86 separately.
description: Control how the assembler should align branches with NOP. If the boundary's size is not 0, it should be a power of 2 and no less than 32. Branches will be aligned to prevent from being across or against the boundary of specified size. The default value 0 does not align branches.

name: x86-br-merging-base-cost
rationale: Instruction, register, cache and ABI properties differ by CPU; use target-specific costs and measure ARM and x86 separately.
description: Sets the cost threshold for when multiple conditionals will be merged into one branch versus be split in multiple branches. Merging conditionals saves branches at the cost of additional instructions. This value sets the instruction cost limit, below which conditionals will be merged, and above which conditionals will be split. Set to -1 to never merge branches.

name: x86-br-merging-ccmp-bias
rationale: Instruction, register, cache and ABI properties differ by CPU; use target-specific costs and measure ARM and x86 separately.
description: Increases 'x86-br-merging-base-cost' in cases that the target supports conditional compare instructions.

name: x86-br-merging-likely-bias
rationale: Instruction, register, cache and ABI properties differ by CPU; use target-specific costs and measure ARM and x86 separately.
description: Increases 'x86-br-merging-base-cost' in cases that it is likely that all conditionals will be executed. For example for merging the conditionals (a == b && c > d), if its known that a == b is likely, then it is likely that if the conditionals are split both sides will be executed, so it may be desirable to increase the instruction cost threshold. Set to -1 to never merge likely branches.

name: x86-br-merging-unlikely-bias

description: Decreases 'x86-br-merging-base-cost' in cases that it is unlikely that all conditionals will be executed. For example for merging the conditionals (a == b && c > d), if its known that a == b is unlikely, then it is unlikely that if the conditionals are split both sides will be executed, so it may be desirable to decrease the instruction cost threshold. Set to -1 to never merge unlikely branches.
